subject.title: [Feature]: deterministic context injection for bootstrap files and session-type filtering

question: Should OpenClaw add a public bootstrap selector and command-expansion contract for this issue now, and which parts should be accepted together versus left to narrower existing PRs?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the remaining behavior chooses public config/API shape, command-execution security boundaries, prompt-cache behavior, and overlap with multiple open bootstrap PRs.

options.title: Design One Bootstrap Selection Contract
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical decision point, then sponsor or replace the open partial PRs under one documented selector/security model.

options.title: Land Narrow Pieces Separately
options.body: Review the tiered and exact-session PRs independently while leaving command expansion and every-session time context as separate follow-up decisions.

options.title: Decline Command Expansion In Core
options.body: Keep bootstrap files static, steer dynamic context through hooks/skills/tools, and only accept safer filtering/time-context improvements.

recommendation.title: Design One Bootstrap Selection Contract
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the canonical decision point, then sponsor or replace the open partial PRs under one documented selector/security model.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest feature-history signal on subagent bootstrap limiting and date/time context, plus prior review context on the related canonical issue path.
